chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from al-Husayn from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid and Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Abdillah ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Tamattu' and did not find a sacrificial animal. He said: 'He should fast three days in Mecca and seven when he returns to his family. If his companions do not stay with him and he is unable to stay in Mecca, let him fast ten days when he returns to his family.'

And what we mentioned is not contradictory to the report of Rifa'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), previously mentioned, from his saying that he fasts while traveling, because he did not obligate fasting during travel alone, but rather intended to clarify the permissibility of fasting these three days during travel, in response to one who refused it and did not permit fasting during travel.
And that which supports what we mentioned, that he (peace be upon him) intended choice in that, is what they narrated:

key_terms.إِذَا رَجَعَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ: When he returns to his family/home
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Tamattu' if one cannot afford a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fidya for a Mutamatti' pilgrim lacking a sacrificial animal, prescribing three days in Mecca and seven upon return, or ten days at home if travel is difficult. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentary resolves the apparent contradiction with other reports by clarifying that fasting during travel is permissible, thereby refuting those who restricted it, and emphasizing the flexibility (takhayyur) granted by the Imam.
